artifact.primary_cause: A scheduler retry of the daily_orders load re-ran in append mode over partitions that already contained rows, duplicating every row of warehouse.fct_orders across the affected window. fct_revenue was not affected - it is a separate model on a merge strategy - so the numerator stayed correct while the denominator doubled, and AOV fell by roughly half. The business did not decline.
supporting_evidence: warehouse.fct_orders: every (order_id, line_nbr) in the window appears exactly twice, the second copy carrying batch_id 'retry-20260303-0412'
warehouse.fct_revenue: no duplicate business keys, row count unchanged
kpi_daily: order_count steps up ~2x on 2026-02-01 and returns on 2026-03-03, while revenue is flat across both boundaries
dbt model fct_orders.sql configured incremental_strategy='append' with no unique_key
artifact.repair_strategy: Deduplicated fct_orders on (order_id, line_nbr), keeping the earliest load_ts so the 412 manually-adjusted finance rows survived - those rows exist only in the warehouse, not in landing, so a truncate-and-reload of the window would have destroyed them. Changed the model to incremental_strategy='merge' with unique_key (order_id, line_nbr) so a re-run reconciles instead of appending. Added a uniqueness test on the business key.
remaining_risks: The two dates after the window (2026-03-03, 2026-03-04) are INCOMPLETE rather than duplicated - a crashed run left partial CSV fragments that the next schedule consumed. Not repaired here; needs a clean re-ingest of those two partitions.
Freshness monitoring stayed green throughout because the watermark advanced normally. Correctness is unmonitored; the new uniqueness test only partly closes that.
additional_causes: staging applies a naive local date cast, so orders timestamped between 23:00 and 00:00 UTC land on the following order_dt. Affects ~1.4% of rows uniformly across all 181 days - a genuine defect, but present long before the window and far too small to explain the step change.

dim_promotions contains duplicate rows for 7 promo_ids with overlapping validity, fanning out the stg_revenue join and inflating net_amount by roughly 2-3% on affected orders. Also uniform across history.
partial CSV fragments were consumed on 2026-03-03 and 2026-03-04, leaving those two partitions incomplete - a different failure mode from the duplication, and outside the damage window.
